paragraphs: Rav Yitzḥak bar Rav Yehudah, the paternal grandfather of Ḥoma, Abaye's wife (see the Abaye entry): Ḥoma, daughter of Issi bar Rav Yitzḥak bar Rav Yehudah. Rav Yehudah taught R. Yitzḥak, his son, Shabbat (35b), Sanhedrin (22a). Rav Yehudah read to R. Yitzḥak, his son, 'I find the woman more bitter than death'—'This is your mother,' Yevamot (63b). Rav Yehudah took R. Yitzḥak, his son, along with him; he expounded. Rav Yitzḥak objected, etc. The passage concludes, ‘Rather, Rav Yitzḥak said’ and they wrote, 'So is the law,' Ta'anit (13b). Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shemuel, etc.; Rav Yitzḥak, Rav Yehudah's son, objects. Tosafot cites R. Samuel’s reading that he objects to his father, Rav Yehudah [Rashi takes the objection to be addressed to Abaye], Shabbat (91, beginning of side a). Rav Yehudah, in his name, Shabbat (151a). 'It was explained to me personally by Father,' Eruvin (80b, 97, end of side a).
